# Solo License - every feature, and where to find it

Solo License is the control layer for coding agents: each kind of action is auto-approved only once it has
proven itself in your repository, and taken back the moment it fails. This page lists everything the product
does today, and where you see it: the **CLI**, the **dashboard**, the **Claude Code plugin**, or the **API**.

**Status key:** ✅ tested and run end to end · 🧪 tested against the agent's documented payloads (not yet run
live with that agent).

---

## 1. Setup

| Feature | What it does | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **One-command onboarding** | `solo-license onboard` finds your agents, previews and writes their hooks, makes this machine's admin token and settings key (macOS Keychain, or a file only you can read), starts the gate, checks it with a harmless read, and opens the dashboard already signed in at the setup guide | CLI | ✅ |
| Per-repo or machine-wide hooks | `init --agent <x>` for one repo; `init --global` for every repo; `--dry-run` previews, `--remove` uninstalls | CLI | ✅ |
| Background gate | `serve --background`, `status`, `stop` (Windows, macOS, Linux) | CLI | ✅ |
| Health check | `doctor`: is the gate up, which agents are wired here | CLI | ✅ |
| Self-install prompt | `prompt --agent <x>` prints a prompt your agent can follow to install Solo License itself | CLI | ✅ |
| Setup guide | Pick your agent, copy its install command, optionally connect neatlogs, Jev and Entire (each with a Test), and watch the first hook arrive | Dashboard `/onboarding` | ✅ |
| Claude Code plugin | `/plugin marketplace add JAYATIAHUJA/Solo_license`, then `/plugin install solo-license@solo-license`; `/solo-license:trust` shows the licenses | Plugin | ✅ |
| Dashboard on the gate's port | the gate serves the built dashboard itself, so onboarding needs no second server | API | ✅ |

## 2. Earned autonomy (the engine)

| Feature | What it does | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Licenses per (repo, action class) | `test-run`, `file-edit`, `install-dep`, `git-remote`, `deploy`, ... ; `npm test`, `pytest` and `cargo test` build the same record | Dashboard (Coding) | ✅ |
| Three levels | L0 asks every time · L1 runs the commands a person already approved here · L2 runs the whole class | Dashboard | ✅ |
| **Promotion** priced by economics | a class climbs only when a floor of verified runs is met **and** the upper credible bound of its failure rate is below break-even (approval time saved vs. cost of one mistake) | Engine, ledger | ✅ |
| **Demotion** | one failure, one over-edited turn, a forbidden attempt or a person's flag drops the class to L0 | Engine, ledger | ✅ |
| Only real yeses build trust | a person's approval or an earned allow is credited; what an agent's own settings let through is *observed*, never credited | Engine | ✅ |
| Hard denies | `rm -rf ~`, `curl … \| sh`, force-push to main, `sudo`, `DROP DATABASE` are never allowed, at any level | Engine | ✅ |
| Chained commands | judged by their riskiest part (`npm test && git push -f` is a force-push) | Engine | ✅ |
| Never fails open | if the gate is down, every hook defers to the agent's own settings | Hooks | ✅ |
| Resume | a person resumes a paused class at the level they choose | Dashboard | ✅ |

## 3. The end-of-turn check

| Feature | What it does | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Over-editing | the turn's diff is graded 1-5 against the request (Jev when a key is set, size-and-spread rules otherwise); 2 or less sends the turn back with the files to revert | Agent, dashboard | ✅ |
| Tests, regression only | the repo's tests run in a throwaway worktree; failing tests are compared by name against the turn's own start, so pre-existing failures are not blamed | Agent, dashboard | ✅ |
| Rewind | a failed turn's changes are stashed (never deleted) and the tree returns to the turn's start | Dashboard (Rewind button) | ✅ |

## 4. The control layer

| Feature | What it does | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remediation | every denial and failure tells the agent what to undo (`git checkout -- package.json package-lock.json`, the checkpoint to rewind to), in the agent's own hook format | Agent | ✅ |
| **"This was wrong"** | flag any decision or turn: its class drops to L0 and the agent hears it on its next prompt | Dashboard | ✅ |
| Live levels + kill switch | levels animate as they change; **Freeze all** makes every action ask | Dashboard | ✅ |
| Subagents | the main agent and each subagent type keep their own license; subagents start capped at `[subagents] max`, can be denied by type, and are checked at their own stop | Engine | ✅ |
| Loop detection | 3 identical calls get guidance, 5 are denied, the same failure 3 times says "stop retrying", a file edited 4 times in a turn is sent back; a new prompt starts the count again | Agent | ✅ |
| Session digest | Jev judges a risky command against the session's goal and the policy (a bounded digest, never the raw transcript) and asks a person when unsure | Engine | ✅ |
| MCP tool classes | each MCP server is its own class (`mcp:github`); reads can earn L2, writes L1, merge / delete / deploy always ask; the policy can forbid or cap a tool | Engine, dashboard | ✅ |
| Policy as code | `.solo-license/policy.toml`, committed with the repo, can only make the agent ask more; `policy init` writes a starter | CLI, dashboard (Settings) | ✅ |

## 5. Money

| Feature | What it does | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Budget caps | `[budget]` caps USD per session and per day, from the agent's own reported cost or an estimate from its transcript's tokens; past a cap only reading is allowed | Engine | ✅ |
| Budget page | today's spend per repo against the cap, recent sessions, who is stopped, **Resume** | Dashboard (Budget) | ✅ |
| `solo-license budget` | the same in the terminal | CLI | ✅ |
| Savings | prompts you did not answer, developer time and $ saved by earned autonomy | Dashboard | ✅ |

## 6. Evidence: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai

| Feature | What it does | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **neatlogs traces** | one trace per turn: `turn.start → gate.allow/ask/deny → tool.ran/failed → remediation.sent → license.promote/demote → turn.end`; denials, demotions, loops and budget stops are error spans, so they show as incidents | neatlogs, dashboard links | ✅ with a key |
| Local trace mirror | without a key, every span is kept in the local database | CLI `explain` | ✅ |
| **Trace links** | each turn and decision in the dashboard and each change in the history links to its neatlogs trace | Dashboard | ✅ |
| **`solo-license explain [turn]`** | one turn's whole story: decisions, what the agent was told, license changes with ledger commits, the trace timeline, the Entire checkpoint, how to rewind | CLI | ✅ |
| **Entire checkpoints** | a failed turn is linked to the agent's last Entire checkpoint (`entire checkpoint explain <id>`) | Dashboard, CLI | ✅ with the Entire CLI |
| **License ledger** | every promote, demote, flag, resume and budget stop is a git commit: `git log -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl` | git, Entire | ✅ |
| Entire Trails + Gates | every pull request in this repository went through Entire Trails and the Entire Gates check | Entire | ✅ |
| **cfo.ai model** | per-developer cost of asking every time vs. full access vs. Solo License, pricing, unit economics, runway: `make cfo` | `planning/cfo/` | ✅ |

## 7. Agents

| Agent | Wired through | Earns trust from a person's yes | Sends a bad turn back |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code (also GLM via z.ai) | HTTP hooks / plugin | ✅ PermissionRequest | ✅ |
| OpenAI Codex CLI | command hooks | ✅ PermissionRequest | ✅ |
| **OpenCode** (Groq, GLM, free models) | plugin | 🧪 `permission.ask` | records it |
| Cursor | command hooks | observed | ✅ |
| Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Grok Build | command / HTTP hooks | observed | ✅ |
| Windsurf, Kiro, Cline | command hooks / scripts | observed | records it |

Every agent loses trust on a failure. "Observed" means the agent's hook fires on every call, so Solo License
cannot tell a person's yes from the agent's own settings; it never credits those calls.

## 8. Security

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| Roles | `operator` < `approver` < `admin`; flags, resumes and rewinds need an approver |
| Local admin | made by `onboard`; the sign-in link carries the token in the URL hash only, and the dashboard removes it |
| Encrypted keys | neatlogs and Jev keys are stored encrypted; never shown back in full |
| Hook paths | paths a shell would expand are refused; hooks from other machines need `X-Solo-Hook-Key` |
| Background stop | never stops a process it cannot confirm is the gate (pid reuse) |

#70 merge ho gaya. CI ke Backend aur Frontend dono green the, aur Entire Gates ka wait nahi kiya. Ab landing page par:
- **Product tour:** CLI, dashboard, Budget, neatlogs aur Entire ke mockups, jo scroll ke saath zoom karke important hissa highlight karte hain.
- **Chhota page:** repeat hone wale 6 scenes hata diye. Ab Hero → In your agent → The crash → Product tour → Facts → FAQ.
- **Install ka alag page:** `/install`, jisme sabse upar `solo-license onboard` hai.

Mobile aur desktop dono par check kiya. Par aakhri do chapters (neatlogs, explain) ka visual sirf DOM se confirm hua, screenshot se nahi, kyunki app window peeche hone par screenshot timeout ho rahe the. Ek baar tum khud scroll karke dekh lena.

## cfo.ai dashboard ka prompt
Ye cfo.ai mein paste karo. Numbers `planning/cfo/coding_business_model.md` se liye hain:

```text
Build a financial model and dashboard for "Solo License", a developer tool that sits in a coding agent's hooks (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) and auto-approves each kind of action only once it has proven itself in that repo; one failure takes it back.

Per-developer assumptions (make each an editable input):
- Developer cost $75/hour; 40 permission prompts/day in "ask before changes" mode; 1 minute per prompt; 20 working days/month
- 5 over-edited turns/week, 12 minutes review each
- Destructive incidents with full access: 0.05/month, $600 each
- Solo License: 75% of prompts answered by earned licenses, 90% of over-edits caught, 90% of incidents prevented

Show cost per developer per month for three modes: ask-every-time ($1,300), full access ($330), Solo License ($283), split into approval time, over-edit review and incident risk.

Pricing: Free plugin; Team $15/developer/month; Enterprise custom.
Unit cost per developer: Jev $0.08 + hosting $0.40 = $0.48 (96.8% gross margin).
Company: fixed costs $4,000/month, cash $25,000, 50 paying seats at launch growing 30%/month.

Dashboard pages:
1. Scenario controls (seat growth, price, % prompts earned, incident cost) with live recalculation
2. Customer value: savings per developer vs ask-every-time ($1,017) and vs full access ($47), and value/price multiple (~68x)
3. 12-month P&L: seats, MRR, COGS, gross margin, fixed costs, monthly profit
4. Cash and runway: cash balance by month, low point, break-even seats (~276) and month (~8)
5. Scenario scorecard: Base, Conservative (50% earned, 15% growth), Aggressive (40% growth), Price $10 vs $20 - side by side

Keep it clean and executive-ready, one headline number per card.
```

## Entire aur neatlogs ke screenshots kab lene hain
Sabse pehle `.env` mein `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` daal ke gate restart karo. Bina key ke traces sirf local rehte hain, aur neatlogs khaali dikhega.

| Kab | Kahan | Kya capture karna hai |
|---|---|---|
| Demo session ke **turant baad** (Claude Code se tests chalwao, phir `npm install left-pad` fail karwao, phir force-push try karo) | neatlogs → Traces | Fail hua turn ka trace: `tool.failed`, `remediation.sent`, `license.demote` (lal spans) |
| Usi waqt | Dashboard → Coding page | Turn row par "Trace in neatlogs" link, aur L0 par gira hua card |
| Usi waqt | Terminal | `solo-license explain` ka output: trace link aur Entire checkpoint |
| Kisi bhi merged PR par (jaise #59 ya #70) | entire.io → Trails | Gates panel (Checks, Findings, Approvals) aur review findings |
| Demotion ke baad | Terminal ya entire.io | `git log -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl` mein demote commit, aur `entire checkpoint explain <id>` |
| Budget cap hit hone ke baad | Dashboard → Budget aur `solo-license budget` | Stopped session aur Resume button |

Entire checkpoint tabhi link hoga jab demo repo mein `entire enable` chala ho, isliye demo shuru karne se pehle use chala lena.

Sorry, galti meri thi. Maine animated scenes ko bhi "repeat" maan ke hata diya. Ab hataye gaye **animated** scenes wapas la raha hoon:
- Problem (over-edit)
- Journey / How it earns (pinned license card)
- AgentGraph (The loop)
- LedgerTrack (ledger ki horizontal track)

Sirf static list wale Detections aur Remediation hate rahenge; unki baat tour aur `explain` mein aa chuki hai. Page zyada lamba na ho, isliye scenes ki scroll-length thodi kam karunga. Animation wahi rahegi.

"""The five behaviours a judge (or an attacker) checks first. Each was either a
real hole or a headline claim; each is pinned here so it cannot regress."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import subprocess

import pytest

from sololicense.coding import shim
from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command
from sololicense.coding.gate import CodingGate
from sololicense.coding.jev import JevClient
from sololicense.db.repositories import agent as agent_repo
from sololicense.services.git_ledger import GitLedger


@pytest.fixture
def gate(harness, tmp_path):
    project = tmp_path / "shop-api"
    project.mkdir()
    for args in (["init", "-q"], ["config", "user.name", "T"], ["config", "user.email", "t@e.c"]):
        subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=project, check=True)
    (project / "README.md").write_text("demo\n")
    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "."], cwd=project, check=True)
    subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-qm", "init"], cwd=project, check=True)
    gate = CodingGate(harness.conn, harness.tracer, GitLedger(repo_root=harness.repo),
                      jev_client=JevClient(), checkpoint_lookup=lambda cwd, session: None)
    gate.project = project
    return gate


def _bash(gate, command, **extra):
    return {"session_id": "s1", "cwd": str(gate.project), "tool_name": "Bash",
            "tool_input": {"command": command}, "_prompt_only": True, **extra}


def _decision(answer):
    return ((answer.get("hookSpecificOutput") or {}).get("decision") or {})


@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", [
    "echo pwned >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys",
    "tee -a ~/.bashrc",
    "cp key ~/.ssh/id_rsa",
    "echo $PATH > /etc/environment",
])
def test_writing_credentials_or_startup_files_is_never_a_read(command):
    result = classify_command(command)
    assert result.action_class != "read"
    assert result.hard_deny == "writes to credentials or shell start-up files"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", ["echo x > notes.txt", "cat a.txt >> b.txt", "sed -i s/a/b/ app.js"])
def test_a_redirect_into_a_file_is_an_edit(command):
    assert classify_command(command).action_class == "file-edit"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", ["npm test 2>&1", "npm test > /dev/null", "echo 'a > b'", "ls -la"])
def test_harmless_redirects_and_quotes_stay_what_they_were(command):
    assert classify_command(command).action_class in ("read", "test-run")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", [
    "git push origin +main", "git push origin +HEAD:main", "git push -f origin main",
    "git push --force origin main", "git push --force-with-lease origin master",
])
def test_every_way_to_force_push_main_is_denied(gate, command):
    gate.user_prompt({"session_id": "s1", "cwd": str(gate.project), "prompt": "ship it"})
    decision = _decision(gate.permission(_bash(gate, command)))
    assert decision["behavior"] == "deny"
    assert "force-pushes a protected branch" in decision["message"]  # a reason the agent can act on


def test_three_approved_verified_runs_earn_npm_test_and_the_fourth_runs_alone(gate):
    gate.user_prompt({"session_id": "s1", "cwd": str(gate.project), "prompt": "run the tests"})
    for _ in range(3):
        assert _decision(gate.permission(_bash(gate, "npm test"))).get("behavior") != "allow"
        gate.tool_result(_bash(gate, "npm test"), failed=False)  # it ran, so the person said yes
    assert agent_repo.get_license(gate.conn, "shop-api", "test-run")["level"] >= 1
    assert _decision(gate.permission(_bash(gate, "npm test")))["behavior"] == "allow"


def test_a_gate_that_is_down_defers_and_never_allows(monkeypatch, capsys):
    monkeypatch.setenv("SOLO_LICENSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:9")  # nothing listens here
    monkeypatch.setenv("SOLO_HOOK_TIMEOUT", "2")
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", io.StringIO(json.dumps(
        {"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "git push --force origin main"}})))
    assert shim.main(["hook.py", "codex", "PermissionRequest"]) == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "allow" not in out  # no answer at all: the agent's own settings decide

# How Solo License uses Entire

Entire is used in two ways: as the **audit trail of the product** (every change to what the agent
may do is a git commit) and as the **record of how the product was built** (checkpoints of the AI
coding sessions, and Trails that gate every pull request).

## 1 · Every permission change is a commit

The licence service writes each promote / pause / resume to
[`ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`](../ledger/license_ledger.jsonl) and commits it with the reason, the
run id and the neatlogs trace id. Entire can explain any of them.

```bash
git log --oneline -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl    # 31 commits at the time of writing
git show <sha> -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl       # the reason, run and trace behind one change
entire checkpoint explain <sha>                     # the session behind it, when one is linked
```

## 2 · Checkpoints of the build sessions

Commits made with Entire's git hooks carry an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer that links the code to
the AI session (prompts, transcript, files) that produced it.

| Commit | Checkpoint |
|---|---|
| `87ab58d` fix(app): evidence page tells the recovery story; screenshots for the README | `01M4N1QZY7KGEB08SN5PEKZR1C` |

```bash
entire checkpoint list
entire checkpoint explain 87ab58d
entire why sololicense/agent/worker.py:351      # provenance of one line
```

Some earlier commits on these branches have no trailer: Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` hook stalled
when commits were made from Git Bash on Windows, and the commits were completed without it.
Commits made from PowerShell carry the trailer.

## 3 · Trails gate every pull request

Runners and Trails are enabled on the repository. Each pull request gets an **Entire Gates** check
(approvals, CI checks, agent findings, up to date):

| Pull request | Trail |
|---|---|
| #8 Score autonomy policies on τ-bench retail | [trail 2](https://entire.io/gh/JAYATIAHUJA/Solo_license/trails/2) |
| #9 Ticket agent with recovery, Stripe/CSV connectors, inbox and earned trust | [trail 3](https://entire.io/gh/JAYATIAHUJA/Solo_license/trails/3) |
| #10 Evidence pack: before/after recovery with paired neatlogs traces | [trail 4](https://entire.io/gh/JAYATIAHUJA/Solo_license/trails/4) |

### Capturing evaluated Trail evidence

For judge evidence, capture a Trail only **after** its Entire Gates have evaluated the pushed
commit. A useful screenshot shows the Trail title and branch, the commit or diff, and populated
Gates for findings, checks, and up-to-date status. A Trail that was merged before evaluation may
show `Not checked`; that is audit history, but not runner evidence.

```bash
entire trail list --status any
entire trail create                 # create a Trail for the current evidence branch
git push origin <branch>            # runners trigger from the push
```

Wait for the Trail page to report the runner outcomes before merging. The expected clean result
for a documentation-only change is no findings, rather than an empty, unevaluated Gates panel.

## 4 · Entire Graph: what the recovery path touches

`entire graph` (plugin v0.4.0) indexes the repository and answers structural questions before a
change. Searching in plain words finds the recovery path first, with its covering tests:

```bash
entire graph search --repo . --query "recover a failed refund" --profile full
```

`RefundWorker._run_refund`; suggested check:

(2 more covering tests: `test_worker_recovers_a_lost_stripe_refund`,

```bash

```

Blast radius: 3 callers (2 direct, 1 transitive), 2 callees, 2 type consumers, 1 data flow, 25 co-change files, 12 siblings.

## What
Re-verified every known weakness against `main`, fixed what was still broken:

| Weakness | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `echo pwned >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` | classified **read** | file-edit **and hard-denied** ("writes to credentials or shell start-up files": `.ssh/`, `.aws/`, `.gnupg/`, `.kube/`, `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, shell rc/profile, `authorized_keys`, `/etc/`) |
| `echo x > file`, `cat a >> b`, `sed -i`, `tee` | read / unknown | **file-edit** (a redirect into a file is an edit, whatever program writes it; `2>&1`, `> /dev/null` and quoted `>` are unchanged) |
| `git push origin +main`, `+HEAD:main` | git-remote, allowed by license | **hard-denied** like `--force` (also `--force-if-includes`) |
| `make coding-benchmark` crash | fixed in #66 | runs |
| Makefile bare `python` | `python` | `python3` where it exists, else `python` |
| Ledger evidence | `ledger/license_ledger.jsonl` held v1 refund history; the coding ledger was in a git-ignored path | v1 history moved to `evidence/history/v1-refund-ledger.jsonl`; the benchmark now also writes the replay's ledger and its commits to `evidence/benchmarks/coding_ledger.jsonl` / `coding_ledger_commits.txt` |
| `evidence/README.md`, `evidence/entire.md` | referenced deleted v2 files and refund code | rewritten for v3: real trails (#54/48, #64/58, #65/59), a real checkpoint trailer (`408592b`), `entire graph impact` on `CodingGate._fail` |
| Digest `turn` fields | always empty | `files_touched`, `failures` and `diff_stat` from the turn's own decisions |

The benchmark was re-run: same numbers (21 -> 11 prompts, 19 earned, 3 force-pushes denied, 157 -> 0 over-edited lines). Its report now says traces were kept locally (no neatlogs key here); README says the replay sends traces when `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set.

## Regression tests (`tests/test_security_regressions.py`, 19)
- writing credentials / start-up files is never a read and is hard-denied
- redirects into files are edits; harmless redirects stay what they were
- every way to force-push main is denied with an actionable reason
- three approved verified `npm test` runs earn L1 and the fourth call is allowed
- a gate that is down defers and never allows
- the digest Jev reads carries the turn's edited files and failures

## Known, not in this PR
- Stop-hook test runs execute inside the API's global lock (`sololicense/api/app.py`), so one long turn check blocks other hook calls.
- The remote hook secret is stored in plaintext in settings (`hook_secret_hint`).

- `python -m pytest -q` -> all pass; `npm test` 45 pass; `npm run build` ok

## Hamari jagah abhi bhi khaali hai?
**Hackathon ke andar haan.** Agent ne 32 repos clone karke code mein grep kiya. Kisi ke paas ye nahi hai: repo × action class ke hisaab se trust, jo verified results (tests, diff scope) se kamaya jaaye aur failure par apne aap chhin jaaye.

Sabse kareeb:
- **kedge:** ek run ke andar tests aur scope check karta hai, par trust yaad nahi rakhta.
- **guardian:** tool call se pehle gate karta hai, par results se kuch seekhta nahi.
- **roster:** promote/demote karta hai, par poore agent setup ka, aur offline. Har action par gate nahi karta.

**Bahar ke open source mein ye idea naya nahi hai.** `Reddytheer/autonomy-ladder` (0 stars) aur `MMVFIRM/UEAL` (17 stars) bhi earned promotion aur revocation karte hain. Par dono coding agents ke liye nahi hain, tests ya diff se verify nahi karte, aur kisi agent ke hooks mein nahi lagte. Ye dono agent ne sirf README se judge kiye, code nahi padha.

To hamara sahi claim ye hai: "coding agents ke liye pehla, tests aur diff scope se verify, 11 agents ke hooks mein enforce". "Pehla earned autonomy" mat kehna.

Vendors: Claude Code auto mode aur Cursor Auto-review dono classifier ya allowlist hain, results se trust nahi kamate.
